name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.34.0 (released 2026-10-24) is the latest release, focusing on experimental cluster improvements: nodes now drain gracefully on shutdown, multiple listen addresses are supported via comma-separated `listen-http` values, and access changes (revocations, deletions) are propagated across all cluster nodes. A security fix ensures all of a user's subscriptions are terminated when access is revoked or the user is deleted (previously only the first subscription was ended, #1845). Recent prior releases (v2.33.1, v2.32.0, v2.31.x) added Go 1.27.3 security build updates, PostgreSQL connection pool metrics, streaming proxy buffering headers, and critical database performance fixes. See release notes at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL (see repo; ntfy uses a dual-license model for the server and clients)
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in October 2026 (v2.31.0 through v2.34.0)
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — user-based access control with topic reservations, permission revocation, and access cache propagation across cluster nodes
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: v2.31.1: Database schema migrated from version 16 to 17 (new index for since=<message ID> reconnects); downgrading to v2.31.0 or earlier requires manually resetting the schema version.
v2.32.0: Each database store now records the oldest compatible schema version — an older ntfy binary will refuse to start on a database migrated by a newer version.
v2.31.1: Start with a warning instead of failing on a newer database schema, changing prior hard-fail rollback behavior.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server, requiring more integration work than ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides a polished cross-platform experience with file sharing and link mirroring features, but it is a closed-source SaaS product with limited free tier and no self-hosting option.

alternatives.name: Ntopng Alerts / Netdata
alternatives.review: Self-hosted alerting built into monitoring tools like Netdata covers infrastructure notifications well but is tightly coupled to their ecosystems, unlike ntfy's generic scriptable pub-sub approach.
